abstract: Under drought conditions, plants conserve water largely by closing stomata, thereby reducing transpiration at the cost of limiting CO2 uptake for photosynthesis. Stomatal opening and closing are driven by changes in guard cell turgor, which depend on fluxes of solutes (K, anions, organic osmolytes) and water. The KAT1 inward-rectifying K+ channel is an important player in determining stomatal movement dynamics and so understanding its regulation and trafficking may contribute to the development of biotechnological tools for breeding or generating drought-resistant plants. To find regulators, we performed a protein-protein interaction screening in yeast. Here, we present the characterization of VAP27-4 from Arabidopsis thaliana, which belongs to the VAP family of proteins associated with VAMPs (vesicle-associated membrane proteins), whose function has not yet been characterized. We confirmed the KAT1-VAP27-4 interaction in planta and show that VAP27-4 acts as a negative regulator of KAT1 in both yeast and Xenopus laevis oocytes. We provide data showing that this putative VAP-type KAT1 regulator has a role in abscisic acid (ABA)-mediated KAT1 endocytosis, consistent with its role as a negative regulator. Importantly, we show the physiological effects of VAP27-4 co-expression on KAT1 function in guard cell turgor and stomatal opening dynamics. Our results support a role for VAP27-4 as a negative regulator of KAT1 involved in ABA-mediated channel endocytosis.
